add-dir.what: Add a working directory for file access during the current session. Type a partial path to see matching directory suggestions; press `Tab` to accept one.
add-dir.when: Give Claude access to another checkout without leaving this session.
add-dir.example: /add-dir ~/work/shared → this session can read and edit that tree too.

advisor.what: Enable or disable the advisor tool, which consults a second model for guidance at key moments during a task. Accepts `fable`, `opus`, `sonnet`, or a full model ID.
advisor.when: When you want a second model consulted at key decisions.
advisor.example: /advisor enable opus → a second model weighs in at key moments.

agents.what: As of v2.1.198, running `/agents` prints a reminder to ask Claude to create or manage subagents, or to edit `.claude/agents/` or `~/.claude/agents/` directly.
agents.when: When you need to create or manage subagents.
agents.example: /agents → reminder to ask Claude to create or manage subagents.

artifacts.what: List the artifacts you own or that are shared with you, then attach one to the session, open it in your browser, or copy its link. Available where artifacts are.
artifacts.when: When a shared artifact should join the current session.
artifacts.example: /artifacts → pick one from the list and attach it to this session.

auto-mode-setup.what: Draft `autoMode.environment` entries from your project and recent sessions, then review the draft and save it to your user settings.
auto-mode-setup.when: When you want auto-mode rules drafted from real session history.
auto-mode-setup.example: /auto-mode-setup → drafts entries, you review, then it saves.

autocompact.what: Set the auto-compact window: how full the context window gets before Claude Code compacts automatically.
autocompact.when: When you want auto-compact to trigger later or earlier than the default.

autofix-pr.what: Spawn a Claude Code on the web session that watches the current branch's PR and pushes fixes when CI fails or reviewers leave comments.
autofix-pr.when: When CI keeps failing on a PR while you work elsewhere.
autofix-pr.example: /autofix-pr → a web session watches the PR and pushes CI fixes.

background.what: Detaches the session to run as a background agent, freeing your terminal.
background.when: Use for long runs you don't need to watch.
background.example: /background “finish the migration” — monitor with claude agents.

batch.what: Decomposes a large change into 5–30 independent units, each in its own git worktree with its own PR.
batch.when: Use for big refactors that would otherwise be one giant, risky change.
batch.example: /batch migrate src/ from JavaScript to TypeScript.

branch.what: Creates a branch of the conversation at this point and switches into it.
branch.when: Use to try a different direction without losing the original.

btw.what: Asks a side question that does not enter the conversation history.
btw.when: Use for quick clarifications that shouldn't pollute the task context.
btw.example: /btw what's the difference between X and Y?

bug.what: Report a bug or share your conversation. You choose how much session history to include and confirm on a consent screen before anything is sent.
bug.when: When something is broken and you want it off your machine.
bug.example: /bug → choose how much history to include, then confirm send.

cd.what: Change the current working directory; relative paths resolve from there. Press `Tab` to accept path suggestions.
cd.when: When the work moves to another checkout mid-conversation.

chrome.example: /chrome → configure Claude in Chrome from the terminal.

claude-api.what: **Skill.** Load Claude API and Managed Agents reference material for your project's language.
claude-api.when: When writing code against the Claude API.
claude-api.example: /claude-api → loads API reference material for your language.

clear.what: Starts a new conversation with empty context, keeping project memory.
clear.when: Use between tasks; label the old one for /resume.
clear.example: /clear “next task” names the previous session in the picker.

code-review.what: Reviews the current diff (or a PR number, branch, or path) for correctness bugs; --fix applies findings.
code-review.when: Use before merge — the correctness gate.

color.what: Set the prompt bar color for the current session. Available colors: `red`, `blue`, `green`, `yellow`, `purple`, `orange`, `pink`, `cyan`.
color.when: When you want the prompt bar color to match a mood or project.
color.example: /color blue → prompt bar turns blue for this session.

compact.what: Summarizes the conversation so far to free context while keeping the thread.
compact.when: Use when the window is full but the task isn't done.
compact.example: /compact “keep the auth requirements” focuses the summary.

config.what: Opens the Settings interface, or sets settings directly with key=value pairs.
config.when: Use for theme, model, output style, and other preferences.

context.what: Visualizes context usage as a colored grid with optimization suggestions.
context.when: Run it when responses start degrading or you're unsure what's eating the window.
context.example: /context shows the grid; /context all expands the per-item breakdown.

copy.what: Copy the last assistant response to clipboard. Pass a number `N` to copy the Nth-latest response: `/copy 2` copies the second-to-last.
copy.when: When a response belongs in a ticket, doc, or message.
copy.example: /copy 2 → copies the second-latest response to the clipboard.

cost.what: Alias for /usage — session cost and plan limits.

dataviz.what: **Skill.** Design guidance for charts, graphs, and dashboards.
dataviz.when: When building charts, graphs, or dashboards.
dataviz.example: /dataviz → chart and dashboard design guidance loads into context.

debug.what: Enables session debug logging and troubleshoots by reading the session debug log.
debug.when: Use when something is failing and you need the log.
debug.example: /debug “why is the tool failing” starts capturing from that point.

deep-research.what: Fans out web searches on a question, cross-checks sources, and synthesizes a cited report.
deep-research.when: Use for questions that need current, sourced answers.

design-login.what: Authorize design-system access for `/design-sync` with your claude.ai account
design-login.example: /design-login → opens the claude.ai authorization flow for design access.

design-sync.what: **Skill.** Convert your repo's React design system and upload it to Claude Design, so designs it produces use your real components.
design-sync.when: When the repo is the source of truth for components.
design-sync.example: /design-sync → uploads the repo React design system to Claude Design.

desktop.what: Continue the current session in the Claude Code Desktop app. Requires macOS or x64 Windows and a Claude subscription. Alias: `/app`
desktop.when: When the terminal session is easier to drive from the desktop app.
desktop.example: /desktop → the session continues in the desktop app.

diff.what: Opens an interactive diff viewer of uncommitted changes and per-turn diffs.
diff.when: Use before committing to see exactly what changed.
diff.example: /diff → arrow through files, Enter to inspect, Esc to return.

doctor.what: Runs a setup checkup that diagnoses installation and configuration issues and can fix them.
doctor.when: Use when things feel broken: PATH, duplicates, stale settings.
doctor.example: /doctor reports findings first, then asks before changing anything.

effort.what: Sets reasoning effort from low to xhigh (or auto/status).
effort.when: Low = fast and cheap; xhigh = deep. Dial it per task.
effort.example: /effort high before a concurrency review; /effort low for mechanical edits.

exit.what: Exit the CLI. In an attached background session, this detaches and the session keeps running. Alias: `/quit`
exit.when: When you are done, or detaching a background session.
exit.example: /exit → leaves the CLI; an attached background session keeps running.

export.what: Exports the current conversation as plain text.
export.when: Use to save a session for later or share it.

fast.what: Toggle fast mode on or off. Availability in non-interactive mode with `-p` is limited; see Toggle fast mode. Requires Claude Code v2.1.205 or later
fast.when: When speed matters more than depth.
fast.example: /fast → toggles fast mode for snappier, lighter responses.

feedback.what: Send product feedback about Claude Code. Opens the same dialog as `/bug`, with the same consent step, sending rules, and mid-turn behavior.
feedback.when: When you have product feedback to send.
feedback.example: /feedback → opens the same consent-first dialog as /bug.

fewer-permission-prompts.what: Scans transcripts for common read-only tool calls and builds a prioritized allowlist.
fewer-permission-prompts.when: Use when permission prompts are slowing you down.
fewer-permission-prompts.example: /fewer-permission-prompts → review the draft, save to settings.

focus.what: Toggle the focus view, which shows only your last prompt, a one-line tool-call summary with edit diffstats, and the final response.
focus.when: When you only need the last exchange, not the scroll.
focus.example: /focus → only your last prompt and one-line tool summaries.

fork.what: Copies the conversation into a new background session while you keep working here.
fork.when: Use to spin off research or a parallel track.
fork.example: /fork “continue this research” starts the copy immediately.

goal.what: Sets a condition Claude keeps working toward across turns.
goal.when: Use for long-running objectives that span many prompts.
goal.example: /goal “all tests pass” — Claude keeps going until green.

heapdump.what: Write a JavaScript heap snapshot and a memory breakdown to `~/Desktop`, or your home directory on Linux without a Desktop folder, for diagnosing high memory usage.
heapdump.when: When debugging memory growth in sessions or tools.
heapdump.example: /heapdump → JS heap snapshot + memory breakdown on your Desktop.

help.what: Shows help and every available command — the catalog's own index.
help.when: Use whenever you forget a command; it's the deck's promise.
help.example: /help lists everything, filterable as you type.

hooks.what: Views hook configurations for tool events.
hooks.when: Use to see what runs automatically around tool calls.

ide.what: Manage IDE integrations and show status
ide.when: When wiring Claude Code into your editor.

import.what: Bring configuration from other coding agents on this machine — currently OpenAI Codex — into your Claude Code setup.
import.when: When migrating from another coding agent.
import.example: /import → pulls config from Codex or Gemini CLI on this machine.

init.what: Generates a starter CLAUDE.md so Claude knows your project's conventions from the first prompt.
init.when: Run it once per repo — it turns a generic assistant into one that knows your build, test, and style commands.
init.example: /init in a fresh checkout writes CLAUDE.md with your project's structure and commands.

insights.what: Generate an HTML report analyzing your recent sessions on this machine: which projects you work in, how you use Claude Code, where things go wrong, and features to try.
insights.when: When you want a data view of your own usage.
insights.example: /insights → HTML report of which projects and workflows you use most.

install-github-app.what: Install the Claude GitHub App for a repository, with an optional step to set up GitHub Actions workflows and secrets.
install-github-app.when: When wiring repo automation to Claude.

install-slack-app.what: Install the Claude Slack app. Opens a browser to complete the OAuth flow
install-slack-app.when: When adding Claude to a workspace.

keybindings.when: When a default shortcut fights your muscle memory.
keybindings.example: /keybindings → opens your shortcuts file for editing.

list-agents.what: List the subagents, agent team teammates, and other Claude Code sessions Claude can message, with the name to use for each. See cross-session messaging.
list-agents.when: When you want to see who Claude can reach and message.
list-agents.example: /list-agents → subagents, teammates, sessions it can message, with status.

login.what: Sign in to your Anthropic account
login.when: When credentials are missing or expired.
login.example: /login → opens the sign-in flow for your Anthropic account.

logout.what: Sign out from your Anthropic account
logout.example: /logout → clears the Anthropic credentials from this CLI.

loop.what: **Skill.** Run a prompt repeatedly while the session stays open. Omit the interval and, where available, Claude self-paces between iterations.
loop.when: When a check should repeat without you retyping it.
loop.example: /loop check CI every 5m → the prompt re-runs while the session is open.

mcp.what: Manages MCP server connections and OAuth authentication.
mcp.when: Use to connect external tools and data servers.

memory.what: Edits CLAUDE.md files, toggles auto memory, and shows auto-memory entries.
memory.when: Use it to refine what Claude remembers about you and the project across sessions.
memory.example: /memory to add “always run pnpm test before pushing” to project memory.

mobile.what: Show QR code to download the Claude mobile app. Aliases: `/ios`, `/android`
mobile.example: /mobile → prints the QR code for the Claude mobile app.

model.what: Switches the AI model mid-session and saves it as your default.
model.when: Use when a task needs a stronger model or a cheaper, faster one.
model.example: /model sonnet, or /model to open the picker.

passes.what: Share a free week of Claude Code with friends. Only visible if your account is eligible
passes.when: When your account is eligible to share a free week.
passes.example: /passes → share a free week, if your account is eligible.

permissions.what: Manages allow, ask, and deny rules for tool permissions.
permissions.when: Set it once per project so read-only commands run without prompts while destructive ones still ask.
permissions.example: /permissions → allow git status, ask for rm -rf.

plan.what: Enters plan mode: Claude researches and proposes before editing anything.
plan.when: Use before large changes so the approach is agreed before code moves.
plan.example: /plan fix the auth bug → Claude investigates, proposes, you approve.

plugin.what: Manages Claude Code plugins: list, install, enable, disable.
plugin.when: Use to extend the CLI with marketplace plugins.

powerup.what: Discover Claude Code features through quick interactive lessons with animated demos
powerup.when: When learning Claude Code features by doing.
powerup.example: /powerup → quick interactive lessons with animated demos.

pr-comments.what: Removed in v2.1.91 — ask Claude directly to view PR comments instead.
pr-comments.example: Ask: “what comments are on this PR?”

privacy-settings.what: View and update your privacy settings. Only available for Pro and Max plan subscribers
privacy-settings.when: When reviewing what data leaves your machine.

radio.what: Open Claude FM lo-fi radio in your browser. Prints the stream URL when no browser is available.
radio.when: When a little lo-fi helps the long grind.
radio.example: /radio → lo-fi stream opens in your browser; URL printed if not.

rate-limit-options.what: Show ways to keep working when a claude.ai usage limit blocks a request: wait and continue automatically when the limit resets, add usage credits, or upgrade your plan.
rate-limit-options.when: When claude.ai shows a usage limit block.
rate-limit-options.example: /rate-limit-options → ways to keep working when a limit hits.

recap.what: Generate a one-line summary of the current session on demand. See Session recap for the automatic recap that appears after you've been away
recap.when: When someone asks what this session did.
recap.example: /recap → one-line summary of the session so far, on demand.

release-notes.what: View the changelog in an interactive version picker. Select a specific version to see its release notes, or choose to show all versions.
release-notes.when: When checking what changed in a version.

reload-plugins.what: Reload all active plugins to apply pending changes without restarting. Reports counts for each reloaded component and flags any load errors.
reload-plugins.when: After adding or editing a plugin mid-session.
reload-plugins.example: /reload-plugins applies pending changes without a restart.

reload-skills.what: Re-scan skill and command directories so skills added or changed on disk during the session become available without restarting.
reload-skills.when: After dropping a new skill into a directory.
reload-skills.example: /reload-skills → re-scans skill dirs; new skills become live.

remote-control.what: Make this session available for Remote Control from claude.ai.
remote-control.when: When you want to drive this terminal from claude.ai.
remote-control.example: /remote-control → this session becomes controllable from claude.ai.

remote-env.what: Choose the default environment for cloud agents
remote-env.when: When cloud agents should start in the right environment.
remote-env.example: /remote-env → pick the default environment for cloud agents.

rename.what: Rename the current session and show the name on the prompt bar. Without a name, auto-generates one from conversation history. Also available in non-interactive mode (`-p`);
rename.when: When finding this session in the picker later matters.
rename.example: /rename auth-migration → names the session on the prompt bar.

resume.what: Reopens a conversation by ID or name from the session picker.
resume.when: Use to continue interrupted work with full context.
resume.example: /resume → pick “fix auth bug” from the list.

review.what: Alias for /code-review — same effort levels and flags.

rewind.what: Rolls the conversation and/or code back to a checkpoint, or summarizes from a selected message.
rewind.when: The undo for both the chat and the files.
rewind.example: /rewind → pick checkpoint 3, files and conversation restore.

run.what: Launches and drives your project's app to see a change working.
run.when: Use to smoke-test real behavior, not just tests.
run.example: /run starts the app and exercises the changed flow.

run-skill-generator.what: **Skill.** Teach `/run` and `/verify` how to build, launch, and drive your project's app from a clean environment by writing a per-project skill
run-skill-generator.when: When /run or /verify mis-launches your bespoke stack.
run-skill-generator.example: /run-skill-generator → teaches /run and /verify your app's launch recipe.

sandbox.what: Toggle sandbox mode. Available on supported platforms only
sandbox.when: When running untrusted code with containment.
sandbox.example: /sandbox → toggles sandbox mode where the platform supports it.

schedule.what: Create, update, list, or run routines, which execute in the cloud. Claude walks you through the setup conversationally. You can also ask about a routine's recent runs.
schedule.when: When a task should run in the cloud without you.
schedule.example: /schedule nightly dependency scan → cloud routine, wizard-led.

scroll-speed.what: Adjust mouse wheel scroll speed interactively, with a ruler you can scroll while the dialog is open to preview the change.
scroll-speed.example: /scroll-speed → interactive ruler to set wheel speed.

security-review.what: Analyzes the branch diff for injection, auth, and data-exposure risks.
security-review.when: Use before merge on anything touching user input or secrets.
security-review.example: /security-review on a branch that adds an API endpoint.

setup-bedrock.what: Configure Amazon Bedrock authentication, region, and model pins through an interactive wizard. Hidden from the command menu until `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1` is set;
setup-bedrock.when: When routing Claude through Amazon Bedrock.
setup-bedrock.example: /setup-bedrock → auth, region, and model pins via wizard.

setup-vertex.what: Configure Google Cloud's Agent Platform authentication, project, region, and model pins through an interactive wizard.
setup-vertex.when: When routing Claude through Google Cloud.
setup-vertex.example: /setup-vertex → auth, project, region via wizard; hidden by default.

simplify.what: Runs four parallel review agents for cleanup: reuse, simplification, efficiency, abstraction level.
simplify.when: Use after a feature lands to pay down cruft.

skills.what: Lists available skills, filterable and sortable by token count.
skills.when: Use to see what skills are loaded and how much context they cost.
skills.example: /skills → press t to sort by tokens.

stats.what: Alias for /usage, opening on the Stats tab.

status.what: Open the Settings interface on the Status tab, showing version, model, account, and connectivity.
status.when: When checking version, account, and connectivity health.
status.example: /status → shows version, model, account, and connectivity at a glance.

statusline.what: Configure Claude Code's status line. Describe what you want, or run without arguments to auto-configure from your shell prompt
statusline.when: When the bottom line should show what you care about.
statusline.example: /statusline show model + git branch → configures the bottom line.

stickers.when: When the laptop needs more stickers.

stop.what: Stop the current background session. Only available while attached to a background session; the transcript and any worktree are kept.
stop.when: When the background session should halt now.
stop.example: /stop → halts the background session you are attached to.

subtask.what: Spawns a forked subagent that inherits the full conversation and reports back.
subtask.when: Use to hand off a side task without losing context.
subtask.example: /subtask write tests for the new parser.

tasks.what: Lists background work in the session, including finished subagents.
tasks.when: Use to check on parallel work without losing your place.
tasks.example: /tasks shows each subagent's status and results.

team-onboarding.what: Generate a team onboarding guide from your Claude Code usage history.
team-onboarding.when: When a teammate needs the working patterns, not the manual.

teleport.what: Pull a Claude Code on the web session into this terminal. Opens a picker, then fetches the branch and conversation. Also available as `/tp`. Requires a claude.ai subscription
teleport.when: When a web session should continue in your terminal.
teleport.example: /teleport → pick a web session; branch and state arrive here.

terminal-setup.what: Configure terminal keybindings for Shift+Enter and other shortcuts. Only visible in terminals that need it, like VS Code, Cursor, Devin Desktop, Alacritty, or Zed
terminal-setup.when: When multiline keyboards shortcuts need custom keys.

theme.what: Change the color theme, including `auto` (matches your terminal background), light, dark, and colorblind-accessible variants.
theme.when: When the terminal colors clash (or the room lights change).
theme.example: /theme dark → switches the session palette (auto follows the terminal).

tui.what: Set the terminal UI renderer and relaunch into it with your conversation intact. `fullscreen` enables the flicker-free alt-screen renderer.
tui.when: When the renderer should match the terminal better.
tui.example: /tui fullscreen → relaunches with the fullscreen renderer.

ultraplan.when: Plan mode does the research-then-propose loop now.

ultrareview.what: Alias for /code-review ultra — deep multi-agent cloud review.
ultrareview.when: Use for the heaviest review; 3 free runs on Pro/Max.

upgrade.what: Open the upgrade page in your browser to switch to a higher plan tier. When the browser fails to open, the command shows a sign-in prompt without printing the URL
upgrade.when: When the plan tier is the bottleneck.
upgrade.example: /upgrade → opens the plan page in your browser.

usage.what: Shows session cost, plan usage limits, and activity stats.
usage.when: Use to keep an eye on spend.

usage-credits.what: Configure usage credits, or request them from your admin, when you hit a limit.
usage-credits.when: When credits run out before the month does.
usage-credits.example: /usage-credits → configure credits or request them from admin.

verify.what: Confirms a change works by building the app, running it, and observing the result.
verify.when: Use instead of trusting tests alone — proof, not type checks.
verify.example: /verify launches the app and drives the changed path.

vim.what: Removed in v2.1.92 — toggle Vim mode via /config → Editor mode.

voice.what: Toggle voice dictation, or enable it in a specific mode. Requires a Claude.ai account

web-setup.what: Connect your GitHub account to Claude Code on the web using your local `gh` CLI credentials. `/schedule` prompts for this automatically if GitHub isn't connected
web-setup.when: When configuring Claude Code on the web from local gh.
web-setup.example: /web-setup → connects GitHub via local gh credentials.

workflows.what: Open the workflow progress view to watch, pause, resume, or save running and completed workflows
workflows.when: When watching or pausing running workflow progress.
workflows.example: /workflows → open the progress view; pause or resume a run from there.
